label: COVERAGE_VERDICTS_rater2
provenance: Blind rater, fresh context, tools forbidden, given PREREG_COVERAGE.md's withholdings: six boards in the order 02/04/08/09/13/K1-to-K3, each with goal, incumbent invariant and move; T3's ORIGINAL pre-patch wording; no classification of mine, no after-boards, no mention of a split or of '(rounds) x (cost per step)'.
transcription: scale_parameter and reason are quoted or closely paraphrased from the rater's own summary table and per-board text. Verdicts are verbatim.

boards.reason: none: the invariant is scale-free in delta -- the recursion is valid at every delta > 0, so the condition holds for all C and carries zero information. The loss's shape is budget exhaustion against iteration count: 1/(c delta) <= n, forcing delta >~ 1/(cn). Two candidate scales (1/delta, the dimension budget n) were named and rejected rather than forced.

boards.scale_parameter: the deviation from 1/2 in units of sqrt(delta) -- the constant C in the target's 1/2 + C sqrt(delta)
boards.reason: matrix Bernstein gives P(||Sigma_S - I/2|| >= t) <= 2n exp(-t^2/(2 delta)), informative only for t >= sqrt(2 delta ln 2n).
boards.flag_raised_by_rater: a reconstrual: a partition is not literally a state satisfying matrix Chernoff at scale C -- the tail bound is a statement about a random process, not a per-state predicate. What is scale-indexed is the certificate's resolution at the target norm. Called PARSES, but as one step of interpretation, not a literal match.

boards.scale_parameter: the discrepancy in units of sqrt(n) -- the constant C in C sqrt(n)
boards.min_C: sqrt(2 ln 2n)(1+o(1)) = Theta(sqrt(log n)), i.e. Theta(sqrt(n log n)) discrepancy
boards.reason: per-set sub-Gaussian tail 2exp(-C^2/2), union bound over n sets informative only for 2n exp(-C^2/2) < 1. The cap is in the composition (per-set tail x n), not in the choice of move.

the invariant is a contraction on a defect with the target as its fixed point, so it holds there vacuously at every scale one might name; the loss is a rate, (1-c)^N, not a threshold. Strained against two scale-looking parameters and rejected both: s, whose critical value k(k+1)/2 belongs to the target's statement and would smuggle the goal in as the diagnosis, and the internal scales X^{1/k}, p^j, which are the move's own.

the invariant is a two-coordinate trade-off in k, the move's own parameter, so any C named is a parameter of the move; and a single PCP instance is not in the invariant's domain. Forcing C = the size exponent runs the other way: for fixed constant soundness k = O(1), so the invariant does not cap the polynomial-size target. The real obstruction is that any k >= 2 gives size >= n^2, a cost-accounting fact about the move that T3's form cannot express.

boards.scale_parameter: the cube half-width (side parameter) C of the target body [-C,C]^n, with the invariant gamma_n(K) >= 1/2
boards.reason: gamma_n(K_C) = (1 - 2Q(C))^n >= 1/2 iff C^2/2 = ln n - O(log log n). At fixed C the target cube has measure e^{-c(C) n}. The move can only shrink measure, so the requirement is already impossible before the move is specified; a measure-preserving, i.e. optimal, move changes nothing.

cross_cutting_caveat_raised_by_rater: On all three boards where T3 parses, min C = Theta(sqrt(log n)), but only on board 6 does 'whatever the move does' hold literally, because there the move is monotone in the invariant. On boards 2 and 3 the cap is a cap ON THE INVARIANT, and it is tight for the incumbent move, so the sound reading is 'no move-side improvement ANALYSED BY THIS INVARIANT reaches O(1)' -- the targets themselves are true (Marcus-Spielman-Srivastava; Spencer).
